citations.quote: ## 6.2.1. Phase 3: Study PVO-1A-301
PVO-1A-301 NCT 03312634	Adult and pediatric subjects ≥4 years of age with FOP	Control type: Historical control

Study PVO-1A-301 (Study 301) was a phase 3 study with the primary objective of evaluating the efficacy of the chronic/flare-up dosing regimen of palovarotene to decrease new HO development in adult and pediatric patients with FOP.

design.text: Single-arm, open-label study with no randomization, using untreated patients from the natural history study (NHS) as a historical/external control.

citations.quote: The Applicant chose to use untreated patients from the NHS as an external control arm.

Control type: Historical control
Randomization: none
Open-label

population.text: Adult and pediatric patients ≥4 years of age with a clinical diagnosis of FOP and no flare-up symptoms within the previous 4 weeks; the principal analysis population required the classic R206H mutation and no prior palovarotene exposure.

citations.quote: Adult and pediatric patients \ge 4 years of age with a clinical diagnosis of FOP and no flare-up symptoms within the previous 4 weeks were eligible to enroll in Study 301.
most of the subjects (i.e., the Principal Analysis population) were required to have the classic R206H mutation and no prior exposure to palovarotene.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint: annualized change in new heterotopic ossification (HO) volume as measured by whole-body computed tomography (WBCT); prespecified primary analysis was a Bayesian compound Poisson model with square root transformation.

citations.quote: The primary endpoint was the annualized change in new HO volume as measured by whole body computed tomography (WBCT).
The prespecified primary analysis for the primary endpoint was based on a Bayesian compound Poisson model.

n.text: 107 subjects treated with palovarotene (Study 301); primary analysis compared 97 palovarotene subjects to 101 NHS controls (P-FAS).

citations.quote: Number treated: 107 Duration: Up to 48 months

result.text: The prespecified Bayesian primary analysis failed: median between-study ratio of annualized new HO was 0.95 (95% CI 0.74, 1.22) with posterior probability of reduction only 0.65. Approval relied on post hoc/confirmatory analyses: using the linear mixed effects model, mean annualized new HO was 9.4 cm3/year (palovarotene) vs 20.3 cm3/year (NHS), treatment difference 10.9 cm3/year (95% CI -21.2, -0.6), nominal p=0.039.

citations.quote: the primary endpoint of annualized new HO failed to demonstrate efficacy of palovarotene with adequate posterior probability

Using the linear mixed effects model, the mean annualized new HO was 9.4 \text{cm}^3/\text{year} in subjects receiving palovarotene (study 301) and 20.3 \text{cm}^3/\text{year} in the NHS with a treatment difference of 10.9 \text{cm}^3/\text{year} (95% CI: -21.2, -0.6).

indication.text: SOHONOS is a retinoid indicated for reduction in the volume of new heterotopic ossification in adults and children aged 8 years and older for females and 10 years and older for males with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP).

citations.quote: SOHONOS is a retinoid indicated for reduction in the volume of new heterotopic ossification in adults and children aged 8 years and older for females and 10 years and older for males with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) (1).

target_moa.text: Palovarotene is a retinoic acid receptor gamma (RARγ)-selective agonist (retinoid); binding to RARγ antagonizes BMP/ALK2 downstream signaling by reducing SMAD 1/5/8 phosphorylation, dampening bone morphogenetic protein signaling and blocking chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation to prevent abnormal endochondral bone formation.

citations.quote: Mechanism of action	Binding of palovarotene to RAR\gamma antagonizes bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) / activin receptor-like kinase 2 (ALK2) downstream signaling by reducing BMP-mothers against decapentaplegic homolog (SMAD) 1/5/8 phosphorylation, potentially by promoting proteasome-mediated SMAD degradation.

Palovarotene is an orally bioavailable RAR\gamma selective agonist (retinoid) that appears to interfere with ALK2-mediated bone formation indirectly by dampening bone morphogenetic protein signaling, leading to blockade of chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation, reprogramming of progenitor cells into nonskeletal lineage, and prevention of abnormal endochondral bone formation in animal models.

modality.text: Small molecule (orally bioavailable retinoid / RARγ-selective agonist).

citations.quote: Palovarotene is an orally bioavailable retinoic acid receptor (RAR) gamma (RAR\gamma) selective agonist (retinoid) proposed for the prevention of heterotopic ossification in adults and children aged 8 years and older for females and 10 years and older for males with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥10%) are dry skin, lip dry, arthralgia, pruritis, pain in extremity, rash, alopecia, erythema, headache, back pain, skin exfoliation, nausea, musculoskeletal pain, myalgia, dry eye, hypersensitivity, peripheral edema, and fatigue. Serious/labeled risks include embryo-fetal toxicity and premature epiphyseal closure in growing pediatric patients.

detail.text: Boxed warning for embryo-fetal toxicity (contraindicated in pregnancy; teratogenic) and premature epiphyseal closure in growing pediatric patients.

citations.quote:
## WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY and PREMATURE EPIPHYSEAL CLOSURE IN GROWING PEDIATRIC PATIENTS
## See full prescribing information for complete boxed warning.

- SOHONOS is contraindicated in pregnancy (5.1, 8.1)
Because of the risk of teratogenicity and to minimize fetal exposure, SOHONOS is to be administered only if conditions for pregnancy prevention are met (5.1, 8.1)
- SOHONOS causes premature epiphyseal closure in growing pediatric patients with FOP, close monitoring is recommended (5.2, 8.4)

vote.text: Advisory Committee met June 28, 2023; 10 of 14 members voted that Study 301 evidence demonstrates palovarotene is effective in FOP, and 11 of 14 voted that benefits outweigh risks.

citations.quote: An Advisory Committee meeting was held on June 28, 2023, to discuss the substantial evidence of effectiveness for palovarotene in the treatment of pediatric and adult patients with FOP.
The majority of the Committee members (10 of 14) voted "Yes," that the evidence from Study 301 demonstrates that palovarotene is effective in patients with FOP.
The majority of the Committee members (11 of 14) voted "Yes," that the benefits of palovarotene outweigh its risks for the treatment of patients diagnosed with FOP.

requirement.text: PMR 4474-3: Conduct a prospective observational registry study comparing palovarotene-exposed and unexposed FOP patients, evaluating risks of increased flare-up episodes, alterations in growth, and bone fractures, and collecting pregnancy exposure outcomes; collect 10-year safety data from a minimum of 100 subjects.

citations.quote: 4474-3 Conduct a prospective observational registry study with safety objectives of comparing palovarotene exposed and unexposed patients with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). Evaluate risks of increased flare-up episodes, alterations in growth, and bone fractures.

The registry should also collect information on women exposed to palovarotene during pregnancy to assess for adverse events related to pregnancy through the first year postpartum, and birth and developmental outcomes through the infant's first year of life.

Collect 10-year safety data from a minimum of 100 subjects, approximately half of whom will be pediatric patients (8 years to less than 18 years of age for girls and 10 years to less than 18 years of age for boys), and approximately two-thirds of whom will be exposed to palovarotene.

summary.text: Palovarotene received orphan drug designation for FOP (July 21, 2014) and Fast Track designation (November 25, 2014). The NDA was reviewed under Priority review as a resubmission following a Complete Response letter dated December 23, 2022, and was approved via traditional (non-accelerated) approval after an Advisory Committee meeting on June 28, 2023, as the first pharmacologic therapy for FOP.
